name: Congenital Symblepharon
aliases: Congenital Adhesion of Eyelid to Globe

criteria.description: Presence of fibrous adhesions between the palpebral and bulbar conjunctiva at birth
No history or evidence of acquired causes such as trauma, infection, or chemical injury
Presence of associated congenital ocular anomalies such as microphthalmia or coloboma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fibrous conjunctival adhesions at birth without acquired causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; histopathology may confirm fibrous tissue adhesion.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fibrous adhesion between palpebral and bulbar conjunctiva
searchTerms: scar tissue between eyelid and eyeball

pathognomonic.symptomName: Restricted ocular motility due to conjunctival adhesions
searchTerms: limited eye movement from eye adhesions
difficulty moving eye due to scarring

common.symptomName: Eyelid malposition related to conjunctival scarring
searchTerms: eyelid turned out or in due to conjunctiva damage
abnormal eyelid position from eye scarring

common.symptomName: Corneal exposure or irritation secondary to symblepharon
searchTerms: dry or irritated cornea from eye adhesions
corneal exposure due to conjunctival bands

common.symptomName: Epiphora due to impaired tear film distribution
searchTerms: excessive tearing from poor tear spread
watery eyes due to tear film problems
tearing caused by eye surface issues

common.symptomName: Microphthalmia as an associated ocular anomaly

occasional.symptomName: Corneal neovascularization secondary to chronic irritation
Visual impairment due to corneal involvement
searchTerms: blurred vision due to eye surface disease
eyelid sagging related to eye tissue damage

rare.symptomName: Secondary amblyopia due to visual axis obstruction
searchTerms: vision loss due to eye obstruction
amblyopia caused by visual axis blockage
open wounds on cornea from irritation

imaging: Ocular ultrasound to assess globe and associated anomalies
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be sporadic or associated with syndromic conditions
other: Histopathology reveals fibrous connective tissue bridging conjunctival surfaces

distinguishingFeatures: History of trauma, infection, or chemical injury
Onset after birth rather than congenital
Autoimmune etiology with progressive conjunctival scarring

redFlags: Progressive conjunctival scarring causing vision loss
references: American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Patterns
